summary: Mostly no. On 1h, every session setting landed the same as random entries, whether price crossed the London, New York, previous-day or Monday levels. The result that holds up is narrow: on 4h, while the pair closed above its 200-day SMA, crosses up through Monday's high and through the previous day's high beat random by 0.70% after 20 candles, and both hold without their strongest stretch.

notes: On 1h, Sessions Indicator gave nothing to separate its entries from random candles. Buying as price crossed down through the London low gave 1,140 entries in 931 separate moves, 0.14% behind random after 20 candles and inside the luck band. The level rule "price above previous midpoint" enters about twenty times as often as the London high cross, but in only about twice as many independent moves, and it also landed inside the band.

Crossing up through Monday's high on 4h beat random by 0.53% after 20 candles, just past the band's edge of 0.52%. That gap rests on four signals between Dec 29, 2020 and Jan 1, 2021, and without them it is chance. Split by trend, the picture changes: above the 200-day SMA the cross was 0.70% ahead, held without its strongest stretch, and showed at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles. Below it, 0.43% sat inside the band, and on daily the pooled 1.44% was the same as random.

The weekday cross up through the previous day's high on 4h was 0.37% ahead pooled, inside the band. In uptrends it beat random by 0.70% and held without its strongest stretch, between Dec 19 and Dec 22, 2023, but it showed at 20 and 100 candles only, not at 10 or 50. In downtrends it was the same as random. Holding above that high on 4h beat random by 0.51%, but 68 SOL entries between Aug 10 and Sep 9, 2021 carry it. On daily that setting had 28 episodes, under the minimum of 30, so it is not judged.

Buying as price crossed down through the London low on 4h did 0.74% worse than random, just past the band's edge of 0.72%. It depends on two signals between Apr 10 and Apr 12, 2024, and without them it is chance, though it stayed worse at 50 and 100 candles. The result sits in downtrends only, where it also rests on two signals, on Jun 1 and Jun 2, 2026. In uptrends it was the same as random.

Shorting a cross down through Monday's low beat random by 2.09% after 20 days on daily. Eight SOL signals between Apr 29 and Jun 10, 2022 produce the gap. Without them it is chance, and at 50 and 100 candles it is chance as well. On 1h and 4h the same short was the same as random.

On 1h, session levels add no timing to a bot's start condition on these pairs, so the take profit and DCA orders do the work. On 4h, a cross up through Monday's high or the previous day's high is worth testing as a filter for a long bot, next to a condition that the pair is above its 200-day SMA. That shape breaks in downtrends, where both crosses landed the same as random. Leave the London-low dip entry out: its 4h result runs the wrong way and rests on two signals.
